content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge uses an open sense of the single Isaiah 7:14 verse as the reason for UNDERDETERMINED, which is the kind of single-verse openness K-S2 governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open.", "room": "The phrase 'leaving the sign's sense open' for Isaiah 7:14, weighed against K-S2's 'the verse is not open': either an open single verse can support UNDERDETERMINED, or a single verse whose words carry two meanings at once is not open and both meanings stand.", "why": "K-S2 forbids making a single verse's open or unstated sense a ground for UNDERDETERMINED and says a verse carrying two meanings is not open, so the judge's 'leaving the sign's sense open' reason breaches the rule."}
